questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next exit. Never stop, back up, swerve across lanes, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, move to the right side of the road and stop. Make room for the emergency vehicle to pass. In heavy traffic, move slowly until you can safely get out of the way.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with no sign of a train. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if you see flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a posted stop sign, a flagger's signal, or a train nearby. If you are not sure whether a train is too close, stop. Never try to race a train.

questions.question: When you change your address, how must you notify the county examiner of drivers?
questions.explanation: You must notify the county examiner of drivers in writing within 30 days. Include your new address, name, and driver license number. If you change your name, you must visit the office in person within 30 days with proof of the change.

questions.question: You are on a divided multilane highway and see an emergency vehicle with signals. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move to create a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to create a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle's signals, slow down, make room for it, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving ability?
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity and reduces safe driving skills. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: Who should wear seat belts?

options.text: All passengers every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: All passengers every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your car should wear a seat belt at all times. Without a seat belt, a person can become a flying object in a crash and injure others in the vehicle.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to whom?
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can lead to collisions. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: If you are in a serious crash, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle and move it off the road if possible. If anyone is hurt, call 911 and help them. Report the crash to police if there are injuries, deaths, or more than $1,000 in property damage (or more than $200 in damage to government property like signs).

questions.question: You must signal for at least ____ before turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: You must signal for at least 100 feet before changing lanes or turning. Signal for a longer distance when driving faster.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours to rest on long trips. If you get drowsy, pull off the road safely and take a nap or stay overnight.

questions.question: What affects how far your vehicle travels before stopping?

options.text: The speed your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your vehicle's speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the pavement.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other traffic is visible.
Signal only if there is visible traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other traffic is visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Make signaling a habit, not something you skip when convenient.

questions.question: If a trailer blocks your inside mirror, you must have:

options.text: An outside mirror on the driver's side.
An outside mirror on the passenger's side.
Outside mirrors on both sides of your vehicle.
A person in the vehicle to guide right turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Outside mirrors on both sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If your trailer blocks your inside mirror, you must have properly sized outside mirrors on both sides of your vehicle.

questions.question: Having a few drinks before driving home is:

options.text: Good because you will miss rush-hour traffic.
Good because it releases tension and makes you safer.
Dangerous because drinks can make you an unsafe driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous because drinks can make you an unsafe driver.
questions.explanation: Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal. Alcohol slows your reflexes, affects your judgment, reduces alertness, and impairs your vision. Do not drive if you have consumed any alcohol.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the alcohol's effects.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can increase the effects of both.
There is no effect because they are different.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can increase the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with medicines can increase the harmful effects of both. One drink while taking cold medicine could affect you like several drinks taken alone.

questions.question: Your headlights must work properly and be adjusted:

options.text: Only when driving in a city.

questions.explanation: Headlights are essential for safe driving at night, in rain, fog, and tunnels. They must work properly and be correctly adjusted at all times.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving in bad weather?

options.text: Sudden weather changes require you to change how you drive.
You should slow down in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles coming fast from behind in bad weather.

questions.explanation: Adjust your driving when weather changes suddenly. Slow down in rain and fog. Be aware of vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for conditions.

questions.question: To ensure your physical condition does not affect safe driving, you should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and have regular check-ups.
Know how medicine affects your driving.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your limitations and only drive when it is safe.

questions.question: An arrogant driver is someone who:

options.text: Is in a hurry and races other drivers.
Does not respect traffic laws or other drivers and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: An arrogant driver races other cars and does not respect traffic laws or the rights of other drivers and pedestrians. Never compete with an arrogant driver. Stay away from them.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:
questions.explanation: Slick roads are dangerous, especially on turns and curves. Go slower when turning in slippery conditions than you would on normal roads.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, you should:

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask another driver for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Drive to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: As a driver, you should:

options.text: Respect bicyclists' rights on the road.
Give bicyclists more space than you think they need.
Yield to bicyclists when crossing a bike lane.

questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as cars. Yield to bicyclists when crossing bike lanes. Give them plenty of space when driving near them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is entering the road from the right.

questions.question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving:
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Try to get out of their way.
Make eye contact with the driver.
Speed up while they are passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to get out of their way.
questions.explanation: Get out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not look at them. Speeding up or blocking them will only make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who goes first?
questions.explanation: All drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The first driver to arrive goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is near.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns that the road may be wet and slippery.
